title: Choose the AI service by input and outcome
points: Images and video → Rekognition; documents → Textract
Speech → Transcribe; text to speech → Polly; languages → Translate
Text insight → Comprehend; conversation → Lex and Connect
Custom models → SageMaker AI; foundation models → Bedrock
diagram: Independent input-to-outcome service cards, not a sequential pipeline.
remember: Choose the data modality and output first.

title: Rekognition analyzes visual media
points: Image and video labels, objects, scenes and text
Face detection, analysis, search, comparison and celebrity recognition
Video person tracking/pathing and content moderation have separate APIs
Identity verification needs consent and a threshold appropriate to the risk
diagram: Image/video source branches into labeling, moderation, face analysis and video tracking.
remember: A detected face is not a verified identity.

title: Moderation threshold and human review
points: DetectModerationLabels returns labels at or above MinConfidence
Lower threshold yields more candidates and more false positives
A human-review range or sample can resolve uncertain cases
A2I remains for existing customers; new designs need another review workflow
diagram: Confidence axis with automatic allow, review and flag decisions; explain threshold calibration.
remember: A confidence score is evidence for a review policy, not a verdict.

title: Transcribe converts speech into text
points: ASR creates a transcript from audio
Automatic language identification helps multilingual input
PII redaction is an optional configured output control
Captions, contact-center analysis and searchable media are use cases
diagram: Audio waveform → language identification → ASR transcript → optional PII-redacted output.
remember: Protect both the audio and the transcript.

title: Polly speaks, lexicons pronounce
points: Text or supported SSML → synthesized speech
Pronunciation lexicons map unusual names and acronyms to spoken forms
SSML can control emphasis, phonemes and pauses, subject to voice support
Attach a lexicon to SynthesizeSpeech; test the selected voice and engine
diagram: Plain text and SSML inputs merge into Polly; optional pronunciation lexicon alters speech output.
remember: Lexicon controls pronunciation; SSML controls supported speech behavior.

title: Translate localizes content
points: Amazon Translate converts text between supported languages
Use cases include websites, applications and document text
Check source language, target support, terminology and human quality review
Translation is distinct from speech recognition and speech synthesis
diagram: Source text → Translate → localized text → reviewer → published content.
remember: A localized release still needs domain and cultural review.

title: Lex and Connect serve different roles
points: Connect receives calls and runs contact flows
Lex recognizes spoken or typed intent with ASR and NLU
A fulfillment step may invoke Lambda and CRM integration
Route unresolved requests to an agent with context and permission boundaries
diagram: Caller → Connect flow → Lex intent → Lambda fulfillment → CRM; escalation branch back to human agent.
remember: Connect manages the contact center; Lex interprets the conversation.

title: Comprehend finds meaning in text
points: Detect language, entities, key phrases and sentiment
Syntax analyzes tokens and parts of speech
Topic modeling groups collections of documents
Analyze customer messages with privacy and quality checks
diagram: Document and email inputs → Comprehend capability cards; outputs include language, entities, sentiment, syntax and topics.
remember: NLP outputs require interpretation in business context.

title: Clinical text needs PHI controls
points: Comprehend Medical extracts medical entities and relationships from clinical text
DetectPHI identifies protected health information in supported text
Notes, discharge summaries, test results and narratives are source examples
S3, transcribed speech and streaming ingestion need scoped access and review
diagram: Clinical sources → protected text processing → medical entities and PHI findings → authorized reviewer.
remember: Detection does not replace healthcare governance.

title: SageMaker AI model lifecycle
points: Prepare labeled training data and select features
Train and tune a model; evaluate on held-out data
Deploy to appropriate inference mode, monitor drift and retrain
Separate experiment permissions, data access, model artifacts and endpoint access
diagram: Data → training → evaluation → deployment → monitored predictions → retraining loop.
remember: Training accuracy alone does not establish production quality.

title: Forecasting: legacy service and current path
points: Historical time-series plus related features can predict demand
Forecast is closed to new customers; existing customers can continue
For new work, assess SageMaker Canvas time-series or SageMaker AI
Avoid historical percentage-improvement or delivery-time guarantees
diagram: Legacy Forecast path beside current SageMaker Canvas/Amazon SageMaker AI path, both consume time-series; no implied migration automation.
remember: Preserve the forecasting requirement while checking service availability.

title: Kendra search and knowledge retrieval
points: Index documents and supported connectors for natural-language search
Rank results using relevance, freshness and feedback controls
Kendra is closed to new customers; existing deployments remain
New solutions can evaluate Bedrock Knowledge Bases for RAG
diagram: Existing Kendra index retrieval versus new Bedrock Knowledge Base retrieval; distinguish search results from generated answers.
remember: Search returns evidence; generation creates an answer from it.

title: Personalize recommendations
points: Historical interactions and item metadata train recommendations
Real-time events update user context; API serves tailored items
Websites, mobile apps and outreach channels consume results
Evaluate cold-start behavior, consent, bias and relevance
diagram: S3 history and real-time events feed Personalize; recommendation API serves web, mobile, email/SMS applications.
remember: Recommendations require data quality and an evaluation metric.

title: Textract extracts document structure
points: PDF or image input → text, handwriting, tables or form fields
Expense and identity document APIs target specialized structures
Store raw documents and extracted outputs under separate access controls
Validate low-confidence fields before downstream decisions
diagram: Document image → Textract → typed structured fields → review → application.
remember: OCR text and structured field extraction are different outputs.

title: Managed AI service comparison
points: Rekognition, Textract, Transcribe, Polly and Translate solve distinct modalities
Comprehend and Comprehend Medical analyze different text domains
Lex/Connect handle conversations/contact routing
Personalize, Kendra, Forecast and SageMaker AI solve recommendations/search/forecast/custom ML
diagram: Four clusters of independent services with official icon labels and precise input/output pairs.
remember: Do not substitute one AI service merely because it contains ML.

title: Foundation model request path
points: Application invokes an allowed Bedrock model using IAM and regional access
Choose a model and inference profile based on capability, latency, cost and residency
Input and output safeguards are configured explicitly
CloudTrail API activity differs from optional prompt/output invocation logs
diagram: Client → app role → Bedrock runtime → selected foundation model → response; separate optional guardrail and logging controls.
remember: Model access, content safety and audit logging are separate settings.

title: RAG ingestion and retrieval are separate
points: Ingestion reads approved source documents, chunks and embeds content
Index stores vectors and metadata with update and deletion lifecycle
Query embeds/retrieves relevant passages before model answer generation
Permissions and citations should correspond to the retrieved source
diagram: Top ingestion lane S3 documents → chunk/embedding → knowledge base. Bottom user query → retrieve → prompt with sources → model answer/citation.
remember: A prompt cannot retrieve a document that was never indexed.

title: Knowledge Base choices and access
points: Managed Knowledge Base manages indexing and retrieval infrastructure
Customer-managed variant gives more control over vector store and parsing
Connector, ACL-filtering and feature support vary by type and Region
Scope data-source role, encryption, network path and retrieval caller
diagram: Two knowledge-base architecture options as alternatives; permissions at ingestion and query boundaries.
remember: Validate document-level authorization before exposing answers.

title: RAG freshness and answer reliability
points: Source updates require ingestion/synchronization and index verification
Handle stale, missing, conflicting and unauthorized passages explicitly
Evaluate retrieval relevance and grounded answer quality separately
Return a safe no-answer or escalation when evidence is insufficient
diagram: Source version → sync → retrieval → grounded response; stale-index and no-evidence branches to correction/abstention.
remember: A fluent answer is not proof of current source grounding.

title: Bedrock guardrails at inference
points: Input and output checks can use configured content and sensitive-information policies
A blocked input prevents usable model inference; output policy can mask/block response
Guardrails do not grant access to tools, data or models
Embedding and reranking models are outside this guardrail path
diagram: User prompt → input policy gate → model → output policy gate → app; separate IAM gate for access.
remember: A guardrail complements authorization; it does not replace it.

title: Model invocation logs and data protection
points: Invocation logging is disabled by default and configured per account/Region
Supported bedrock-runtime calls can log request, response and metadata
Same-account/Region CloudWatch Logs or S3 destination and permissions are required
Retain, encrypt and restrict prompts and outputs as sensitive data
diagram: Bedrock runtime branches optional invocation logs to same-Region CloudWatch Logs/S3; CloudTrail API activity separate.
remember: Logging content creates another sensitive data store.

title: AI service permission boundaries
points: Caller needs only selected API/model, resource and data access
Service roles for ingestion and vector store access differ from end-user authorization
KMS permissions and private networking may be prerequisites
Test denied paths across accounts, Regions and unsupported resources
diagram: Three roles: application caller, knowledge-base ingestion role, reviewer; arrows only for authorized actions.
remember: Scope the identity for each stage of the data flow.

title: Choose the pattern for the request
points: Fixed AI API for specialized extraction, speech or vision
SageMaker AI for trained/custom predictive models
Bedrock direct inference for foundation-model tasks
RAG when grounded private knowledge and citations are needed
diagram: Four independent pattern cards with example, data need, operational control and failure mode.
remember: Start with the required output and evidence boundary.

title: Walkthrough: media moderation review
points: Upload approved media and invoke Rekognition moderation
Set threshold using measured false positives and misses
Route uncertain results to an available human-review workflow
Preserve decision, model version and reviewer outcome
diagram: Media → labels/confidence → threshold branch → review or decision → recorded outcome.
remember: Test policy thresholds with representative content.

title: Walkthrough: accessible contact bot
points: Connect accepts the call and Lex identifies intent
Lambda validates booking request and checks authorized CRM record
Fulfill or transfer to a human with relevant context
Inspect transcript handling, fallback rate and call outcome
diagram: Caller → Connect → Lex → Lambda/CRM; low-confidence branch → human agent.
remember: Fallback is part of the designed customer journey.

title: Walkthrough: extract invoice fields
points: Place source in protected storage and invoke Textract
Extract line items, totals and form keys with confidence
Validate mismatches and review ambiguous fields
Store approved structured output with traceable document version
diagram: Invoice → Textract tables/forms → validation rule → reviewer when needed → approved record.
remember: Do not post an invoice solely because OCR returned text.

title: Walkthrough: grounded internal answer
points: Sync an approved document into the knowledge base
Query with caller authorization and retrieval filters
Provide retrieved passages to the model and return source references
Test an absent document, stale version and unauthorized query
diagram: Approved document → index; query → authorized retrieval → cited answer, with abstain branch.
remember: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately.

title: Walkthrough: train and deploy a model
points: Prepare labeled data with training/validation split
Train, tune and compare against a baseline
Deploy to suitable endpoint or batch inference path
Monitor performance and trigger retraining with approval
diagram: Dataset → train → evaluate gate → deploy → predictions → monitoring.
remember: Only a validated model should reach an endpoint.

title: Cost and availability architecture
points: Account for ingestion, storage, inference tokens and data transfer
Choose provisioned/throughput options only after workload measurement
Review model/feature/Region availability and service lifecycle
Set budgets, retries and throttling behavior for user-facing flows
diagram: Cost drivers grouped by indexing, requests, output tokens and storage; Region availability gate.
remember: A working prototype is not yet an operational cost design.

title: AI architecture exam decisions
points: Visual content moderation → Rekognition with review policy
Clinical PHI → Comprehend Medical; general sentiment → Comprehend
Existing Kendra or Forecast versus new-customer alternatives
Private source grounding → Bedrock Knowledge Bases with access controls
diagram: Four scenario cards each point to a selected service and one disqualifying condition.
remember: Read the input, requested output and customer availability.
